title: Advanced Form Validation with Zod
description: Master Zod schemas, custom error messages, refinements, and showing validation feedback on the client.

slides.title: Beyond Required Fields 🔍
slides.content:
# Zod Superpowers

Zod is a TypeScript‑first schema declaration and validation library. It can:

* Validate types: strings, numbers, booleans, enums.
* Add constraints: `min`, `max`, `email`, `url`.
* Transform data: `trim`, `toLowerCase`.
* Refine with custom logic: `superRefine`.
* Provide custom error messages.

We'll use these to create robust form validation.

slides.title: A Robust Post Schema (lib/schemas.js)
slides.content: Add length constraints, trimming, and custom messages.

quizData.question: What does `.trim()` do in a Zod string schema?

options.text: Checks that the string has no spaces
Automatically removes leading and trailing whitespace before validation
It's not a valid Zod method

quizData.explanation: `.trim()` is a Zod transform that strips extra whitespace, so validation runs on the cleaned string.

slides.title: Displaying Field‑Level Errors 🔖
Updated Action with Field Errors (app/actions.js)
slides.content: Return field‑specific errors to display under inputs.

slides.title: Form with Field Errors (components/NewPostForm.js)
slides.content: Read the errors and show them per field.

quizData.question: What does `result.error.flatten().fieldErrors` return?

options.text: A single string with all errors combined
An object where keys are field names and values are arrays of error messages

quizData.explanation: `flatten()` organizes errors by field, making it easy to display validation messages next to the relevant input.
